subject: TTFT + Streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Subject: TTFT + Streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the quick discovery earlier. Recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on TTFT and streaming behavior: 

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary use: user-facing assistant in customer dashboard (low-latency interactive flows).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~50 concurrent sessions for Phase 1; target throughput ~500 req/s.
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: 150ms median, 300ms p95 (goal: <200ms median if possible).
- Streaming requirements: SSE preferred for web client; WebSocket acceptable. Chunk cadence target: first chunk (token) immediately, subsequent chunks every ~200–300ms to ensure responsive UI.

Open questions we flagged during the call
1) Is the 150ms TTFT requirement measured from browser request or from your edge to our API? We usually measure TTFT as time from request arrival at our edge to first token emitted — helps standardize.
2) Can you share typical request/response sizes (avg prompt length and expected tokens returned)?
3) Any network egress/firewall constraints (IP allowlist or proxy) we should know for Private/Dedicated options?

Proposed next steps
- You: share the SLO spreadsheet + network diagram (helps us size routing and egress).
- Us: run a short POC (simulated traffic) to validate TTFT and chunk cadence on a representative endpoint; provide measurement methodology and results.
- Schedule: propose a 60-min POC sync next week to review results and confirm config — are you available Wed or Thu morning PST?

Attachments: please send the SLO spreadsheet and any infra/network details.

I can loop Marissa (product/serving) to help scope the POC and confirm measurement definitions — cc’d.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Ethan Cho <ethan.cho@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: TTFT + Streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Aditya — great summary. Confirming details and answering your questions below.

Q1 (TTFT measurement): We measure from the browser send to first byte in the browser, but we can provide both client-side and edge timestamps. For procurement we can accept your server-side definition if you provide the mapping.

Q2 (sizes): average user prompt 120 tokens; expected model response 40–80 tokens most of the time, rare long-form responses up to 300 tokens.

Q3 (network): Our infra sits behind an outbound-only proxy; we can either allowlist IP ranges or route via our partner transit. I attached a diagram.

Targets we care about (for SLA discussion)
- TTFT: median 150ms, p95 300ms.
- Throughput: sustained 500 req/s over 10 min, spikes to 1.2k req/s for short bursts.
- Concurrency: 50 sustained; up to 200 burst connections across user base.
- Streaming cadence: first token within TTFT targets, subsequent chunks ~200ms cadence.

Attachments attached: FintechCo_SLOs_20260601.xlsx, infra-network-topology.png

We can do Wed 9–11am PST or Thu 10–12am PST for the POC sync. Please book a slot.

—Ethan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ethan Cho <ethan.cho@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 09:20:10 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT + Streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Ethan / Aditya — thanks for the details and attachments, that helps a lot. A few technical notes and proposal for the POC so we can validate to your numbers: 

Measurement definitions and approach- TTFT: Redwood measures server-side TTFT as time from request arrival at the Redwood edge (post any TLS termination/proxy handoff) to first token byte emitted. To map to your client-side numbers we'll capture both: client-side send timestamp (if provided in header) and server arrival timestamp.

POC config suggestions- Model: start with a compact 8B open model (verified for low-latency) for baseline; compare to 13B quantized config if needed.
- Quantization: int8 or optimized fp16 path can reduce exec latency — we'll include both runs.
- Routing: we can pin traffic to a dedicated pool for this POC to eliminate noisy neighbor effects.
- Batching/caching: set batch window to 10–20ms for interactive flows; enable prefix KV caching if you have repeated context.

Streaming specifics- Protocol: SSE will be easiest to reason about for browser; WebSocket will be similar but we should account for socket multiplexing on your side.
- Chunk cadence: first chunk normally includes the first token(s) and will be the primary TTFT signal. After that we control emission cadence by flush intervals — we'll experiment with 100ms, 200ms, 300ms cadences.

Network notes- Because you sit behind an outbound proxy, please confirm whether our outbound IP allowlist is possible, or if you prefer an agent/connector. If allowlist, we'll share ranges and coordinate security review.

Deliverables for POC (what we will produce)- Measurement methodology doc (so we agree on TTFT/p95/p99 computation).
- POC test harness and load profile to replicate 500 req/s sustained + 1.2k spike.
- Results: TTFT median/p95, chunk cadence histograms, throughput and error rates, and a short set of recommendations (quantization/routing/config).

If that sounds right I can own the measurement plan and POC execution. Aditya, can you confirm customer availability for Wed 9–10am PST?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Serving | Redwood Inference
